aiGuidance.purpose: A passage someone actually read, recorded so a claim can cite words rather than a title. Attach it to the work it came from with derived-from, and to each claim it supports with evidences. Its checked-to level is the level of THIS reading, not of the claim: a passage copied out of a secondary summary is secondary even when the claim it supports is strong. Do not create one from memory or from a search snippet — the wording must be in front of you, because the whole point of a quotation is that a reader can go and check it. Prefer the shortest passage that carries the point; a quotation is evidence, not a substitute for the argument.

description: One passage quoted from a source, with where it was found and how far it was checked. The level between a work and a wording: a source record says which book, a quotation says which words and where.
name: quotation
